summary.headline: Saregama Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR 287 crore and adjusted EBITDA hit a record INR 133 crore (+31% YoY).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 287 crore (+19% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of INR 133 crore (+31% YoY) and operational PBT of INR 105 crore (+37% YoY). Management attributed the Q4 acceleration partly to the exit of Airtel Wynk, which shut in November 2024 and is no longer in the base. Music vertical (licensing, artiste management and retail combined) grew 17% in FY26 to INR 814 crore, with H1 at +8% and H2 at +26%. New content spend was INR 235 crore, below plan, as large films such as Love & War and Paradise slipped into FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY; FY25 included Diljit Dosanjh tour
Below plan; plus INR 105 crore on inorganic catalogue purchases
Management cited FY26 net of other income at INR 73 crore vs INR 37 crore in FY25 (analyst cited INR 7 crore FY23, INR 16 crore FY24, INR 36 crore FY25)

segments.name: Music (licensing + artiste management + retail)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 814 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR 517 crore (+22%), net margin INR 377 crore (+28%). Medium-term guidance: 20-23% revenue CAGR and 60-65% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Video
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 108 crore (-44%), a conscious exit from in-house film production under Yoodlee in favour of the Bhansali Productions stake. Focus is now TV serials and short-format content; no major new projects greenlit.

segments.name: Live events
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 62 crore. Launched first festival IP UN40 (12,000 footfalls, 8 sponsors) with a loss; breakeven targeted FY28. Carvaan Live and US tours planned for FY27.

segments.name: Pocket Aces (digital)
segments.commentary: Reached breakeven in FY26 per management; Saregama owns 91%.

segments.name: Artiste management and brand partnerships
segments.commentary: Managed artists increased to 300+ (about 30 added in the quarter), with over 400 Mn followers. New brand partnerships vertical covers music, live events and short-format video.

guidance_outlook: Music vertical medium-term revenue CAGR of 20-23%; annual music EBITDA margin of 60-65%.
New content budget for FY27 of INR 300-350 crore; FY25-FY27 cumulative around INR 1,000 crore.
From FY28, content investment to rise linearly at high-single to low-double-digit YoY, not in step-jumps; target 25-30% market share of new content.
Music net margins expected to improve 300-500 bps over 3-5 years (management clarified EBIT margin around 46-50%).
UN40 festival to run annually (next edition February 2027); breakeven expected FY28. Video capital allocation to fall to mid-single digits of total capital deployed from around 18%.
Punjabi music push: results expected in 2-3 quarters, possibly by end-FY27 or Q3.
capex_capacity: New content spend FY26 INR 235 crore vs plan; FY27 slate includes Love & War, Naagzilla, Rajinikanth's next Tamil film, Seyon and Paradise.

Strategic minority investment in Bhansali Productions completed in Q4 FY26; valuation linked to its financial performance over three years, giving access to A and B+ Hindi film music for 24-30 months. Its share of profit will be booked via equity method.
Catalogue of about 180,000 songs, adding about 5,500 new releases per year.
Festival UN40 launched in Q4 FY26 as season 1; Carvaan Live small-concert series planned for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says the industry grew 7-8% in FY26 per E&Y/FICCI and IMI; Saregama grew faster, aided by new content.
Platform shutdowns (Resso, Wynk, Hungama, Gaana going fully paid) distorted the denominator; management says this headwind is over.
Paid streaming penetration in India below 3% vs 57% in US; management cites 64% of free users willing to pay if free options stopped.
Short-format video licensing remains one-year fixed-fee deals; social media deals are flat fee.
Q4 financials are affected by timing: society payments come in Q4, and Dhurandhar marketing sat in Q3 with revenue in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Punjabi music weak, and how much will be allocated over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted two past failed attempts in six years. A combined recorded-plus-live deal model is planned, with results expected by end-FY27 or Q3; no allocation figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Were provision write-backs in revenue and do they explain the ~42% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Write-backs relate to royalty provisions and sit in cost of revenue, not in revenue. Q1 provisions unwound in Q4; management asks for rolling 12-month evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 content budget, and what was the impact of Airtel Wynk ending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 new content budget is INR 300-350 crore. Wynk shut in November 2024; customers moved to Spotify, Saavn, Amazon, Gaana, Apple and YouTube.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the music margin step-up (net margin 42% FY25 to 47-48% FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Heavy content amortisation was booked in FY25 (Stree 2, Amaran); FY26 benefits from earlier content with lower charge-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the events business post a loss in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss is mainly UN40, a year-one festival; festivals take 3-4 years to breakeven. Losses expected to shrink year-on-year, breakeven in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unallocable expense increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to lower interest income on the QIP funds deployed into content and Bhansali, which reduces netting off against other income. A detailed reconciliation was deferred offline.

risks_watch: Revenue timing is lumpy: Love & War and Paradise slipped from Q4 to FY27, and management said quarterly swings are normal.
Content amortisation and marketing charge-offs can distort quarterly margins; management asks investors to use rolling 12-month figures.
UN40 and Carvaan Live losses in the events business, plus the Bhansali investment, are unproven for returns.
Unallocable expenses rose sharply (analyst cited INR 37 crore FY25 to INR 73 crore FY26); management deferred a full explanation offline.
ROE is 13.3%, which management said is not satisfactory; the stock has been in a downtrend for several quarters.
Unreconciled point on advances and cash position; the call also raised an IPRS dispute, which management said has no implication.
summary.management_tone: Confident on music growth, the subscription runway and profitability, but defensive and evasive on quarterly comparisons, competitor data, unallocable costs and share price. Management repeatedly asked analysts to use rolling 12-month figures.
key_quotes: Our highest ever adjusted EBITDA at INR 133 crores with YoY growth of 31%
This decline is by design and has not happened by chance.
We are steadfast in maintaining that we will grow it, keeping in mind strong economic principles and never do things which are coming out of vanity.
So, please, every time when you're looking at our numbers, please Saregama's numbers always have to be looked at on a rolling 12-month basis.

growth.why: Medium-term Music revenue CAGR of 20-23% held and FY27 new content budget set at INR 300-350 cr, backed by a named FY27 slate (Love & War, Paradise, Naagzilla, Seyon) and the Bhansali Productions access to A and B+ Hindi film music, but no hard capacity additions and the Music guide is a 3-5 year aspiration rather than a dated commitment.
